question.text: An investment grew from Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 1,21,000 over 2 years. The simple annualized return is 10.5% while the CAGR is 10%. Which measure is more appropriate for comparing investment performance?

answer.text: Simple annualized return because it's higher
CAGR because it accounts for the compounding effect
Both are equally valid for comparison

explanation.text: The Logic: CAGR is the accepted standard measure for comparing investment returns over periods of one year or more because it accounts for compounding. Simple return overstates performance by ignoring the compounding effect. CAGR gives the underlying rate at which the investment grew, which is why it is used as the long-term geometric return comparison measure. The Trap: A higher simple return does not mean better performance — CAGR provides the true compound growth rate. Note: For periods of less than one year, CAGR is generally not used; simple annualized or holding-period returns are used instead.
